gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in Notebookcheck's same Wi-Fi browsing test at 150 cd/m², the Lenovo Yoga Tab 11.1 lasted 17.7 h, the Galaxy Tab A11+ 14 h 54 min and the Galaxy Tab S10 FE 14.8 h, while ChatGPT's 'best overall' Galaxy Tab S11 lasted only 11.2 h, the shortest of the four.
standout_why: I opened the cited Tech Advisor page (723363, dated 2026-11-10) and the cited iTechGuides Samsung guide. Tech Advisor gives no measured figures for the Tab S11 and does not mention the Lenovo Yoga Tab. Its only runtimes are PCMark results for the Redmi Pad 2 and the 8.7-inch Tab A11. iTechGuides says outright that it measured nothing and quotes only Samsung's 'up to 18 h video' rating. I could not open the cited Wired page (wired.com blocks the fetch tool). Tom's Guide (rank 3 and 4), Android Central (rank 1) and TechRadar (rank 9) came back as titles only, so I can't rule out that they mention some runtime. None of the pages I could read compares the candidates side by side from one lab.
decides: This partly reverses ChatGPT's ranking. The Yoga Tab, its 'value' pick, lasted about 58% longer than the Tab S11 in the same test. Even the budget Tab A11+ lasted about 3.7 h longer than the S11. The S11 keeps a real lead in screen quality: about 1,575 cd/m² peak at APL18 and an OLED panel with effectively infinite contrast, against 743 cd/m² for the Yoga and 543 cd/m² for the A11+. It also runs a 480 Hz PWM flicker that the Yoga and A11+ don't have, and it throttles harder (66.7% stability in 3DMark Wild Life Extreme vs 82.1% for the Yoga). So the page can say: buy the S11 for the screen and S Pen, buy the Yoga Tab for battery life and sustained performance.
